name: Improve your balance enough to use a slackline
blurb: Standing on a slackline is a balance skill that carries over to everything else. Nearly everyone can stand on one within a few sessions and walk it within a few weeks.
gear: A slackline kit with ratchet and tree protection
A spotter for the first sessions
steps: Set it up low — ankle to knee height — and tight, with proper tree protection.
Practise mounting one-footed with the line under the arch of your bare foot, aligned along it rather than across.
Fix your gaze on the far anchor, never on your feet, and hold your arms up above shoulder height.
Absorb the wobble by bending the standing knee and letting your arms move freely, rather than tensing.
Practise standing on each foot for 30 seconds before trying to walk.
Walk with slow, deliberate steps, pausing balanced on each foot.
tips: Looking down is the number one reason people fall. Eyes on the anchor.
Barefoot gives far more feedback than shoes.
Always protect the trees, and never set up high without proper training and backup.
proof: You walk the full length of the line, turn round, and walk back.
